Sunshine Always Makes Me Smile. In one of his signature songs, “Sunshine on My Shoulders”, John Denver (God rest his soul) wrote “Sunshine, almost always makes me smile”. As an app, Sunny has provided me with that comfort for years now. The concept and execution of the artwork is superb, and a variety of several scenes (which until recently were in-app purchases) are now included, without additional charge. As in FREE. In my opinion, the artwork is in fact, among the best in the App Store. The soundscape is of high quality, and the ability to customize it, is both user friendly, and incredibly flexible. Whether you use Sunny to relax and unwind from a stressful day, or as a sleep aid, you won’t be disappointed. Given its quality, aesthetic beauty, and very real health benefits, it’s an easy recommendation, and very affordable. Given the current deadly virus that we are all dealing with (I am of course referring to subscriptions), affordability in the App Store is quite a prize indeed.

I would just add that while I’m not familiar with all of the developers apps, I do also own Thunderspace and Windy, both of which I can recommend equally if you enjoy Sunny, and are looking for a little variety.

Childhood vacation revisited. I once spent a week of summer with a friend who lived near the beach in Florida. At first, the ocean sounded so loud! Bliss. I use different scenes for sleep and meditation, sometimes for writing (the thunderstorms app works great for that too) and the incredible realism provided by the way the sounds are put together spatially sets it apart and far above all other similar apps. 

The ironic thing in the reviews is that those people who are flipping out because of one detail or another ["Oh no! Ihat an outrage! I have to pay more for more sound?! Police!!" Why is that so objectionable? Pay a little more, get a little more. What you get initially is worth the price of the app by itself! After a couple of days with the original sounds, I very happily paid a few more dollars to get all the sounds forever and have never been sorry. :) Anyway...] -- those are the people who could probably benefit most from twenty minutes a day of meditation made so much easier and more satisfying with Sunny. 

Ah well -- if you want to be angry, you can always find reasons. But if you're looking for some peace of mind, this is definitely one way to travel. Cheers! And thanks again. :)
